$comment: SHARED City-State agent policy. This file is TRACKED and core-owned: edit it
in the core repository, then `git merge core/master` carries it to every
domain. Before this existed, the same policy was hand-copied into six repos,
which is the exact problem the core/domain split was built to remove.
Personal, machine-specific preferences (model, effort, thinking) belong in
.claude/settings.local.json, which stays untracked and overrides this file.
Restored 2026-07-26 after the mechanism-reachability cleanup deleted it. The
cleanup was not wrong by its own rule - no protocol document references this
file, so it was unreachable in a document graph. It governs what agents may
do, not what documents say, and nothing would have reported its absence. A
deleted fixture turns the suite red; a deleted permission policy is silent
until an agent performs something that should have been refused.
SCOPE LIMIT, measured and important: every rule below is written in
`Bash(...)` form and therefore applies to the Claude Code Bash tool. An agent
that shells out through an MCP server - for example Desktop Commander's
start_process - does not match these patterns at all, and falls through to
whatever the host application decides. This file cannot grant or restrict
that path. Do not read a green rule here as proof that an MCP-based agent is

$comment_allow: Read-only inspection plus the write operations this project actually
performs. `git push` was moved here from `ask` on 2026-07-26 by Human
decision: ordinary publication should not interrupt automation. The
destructive push forms remain gated below.
$comment_ask: Human decision 2026-07-26: history rewriting, worktree destruction and
remote repointing move from `deny` to `ask`. They are no longer refused
mechanically; they require an explicit authorization at the moment of use.
The reason they were denied still holds and is the reason they stay gated
rather than allowed: every domain repository shares an ancestor with core,
so one rewrite of core history breaks mergeability for all of them at once
and nothing afterwards repairs it. `git remote set-url` is here because a
domain silently repointed at another repository is how a push lands in the
wrong system - that trap was found live in the core folder on 2026-07-25.
Approving one of these is a decision, not a formality. Whoever approves it
should be able to say which repositories it affects.
$comment_deny: These are kept as hard refusals because they are unrelated to git

Repository deletion and visibility changes stay denied for the same
